A soil specimen is tested in a triaxial cell. The soil is first consolidated under a cell pressure of 700 kN/m2 with a back pressure of 350 kN/m2. With drainage prevented, the cell pressure is increased to 800 kN/m2, which causes the pore pressure to rise to 445 kN/m2. An axial load is
then applied, producing a deviator stress of 575 kN/m2 while the cell pressure remains at 800 kN/m2. The pore pressure then increases to 640 kN/m2. The correct pair of values for the pore pressure coefficients A and B respectively is :

questions.html: Select the correct statement(s) about behaviour of sands under shear:

An open cut excavation is proposed in the clay from the ground surface. Assuming that uplift failure governs the condition, the safe depth of excavation will be: (Take G = 2.67, = 9.81 kN/m3)

When a cohesive soil is compacted on the dry side of optimum and on the wet side of optimum, the soil behaviour changes significantly. Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the two cases?

options.html: On the dry side of optimum, soil fabric tends to be flocculated showing higher strength at low water contents, whereas on the wet side of optimum, the soil structure becomes dispersed, leading to higher compressibility at low stresses.
On the wet side of optimum, the soil always has lower permeability than on the dry side of optimum however its stress-strain curve shows a steeper rise and sharper peak compared to dry of optimum.

On the dry side of optimum, the swelling potential is higher due to greater water deficiency and random orientation of soil particles, whereas on the wet side of optimum, the soil exhibits greater shrinkages upon drying because of more oriented arrangement of soil particles.

Compaction on the wet side of optimum generally results in higher undrained shear strength after saturation, whereas compaction on the dry side of optimum generally produces much lower undrained shear strength.

questions.html: A standard Newmark’s influence chart is shown in the figure. If the regions labelled A and B are loaded equally, then the resulting pressures at the center will be such that:

options.html: Resulting pressure due to A > Resulting pressure due to B
Resulting pressure due to A < Resulting pressure due to B
Resulting pressure due to A = 4 times resulting pressure due to B
Resulting pressure due to A = Resulting pressure due to B

questions.solution:
(d)
Newmark’s influence chart is constructed so that each small sector has the same influence at the center.
